title: Shadow runner: enforce capacity budgets with rate limiting + queue backpressure
author: Cole Summers
release_notes: - Shadow executions are now subject to per-route + per-project budgets (tokens/sec + in-flight). - When budgets are exceeded, shadow work is dropped or deferred without impacting the primary request path. - New metrics: shadow_eval.queue_depth, shadow_eval.drop_count, shadow_eval.rate_limited_count, shadow_eval.backpressure_ms.
description:
Motivation: Shadow Traffic is explicitly non-impacting; we need hard guardrails so misconfigurations (sampling % too high, too many shadow targets, bursty traffic) cannot consume unbounded GPU/queue capacity. This PR adds rate limiting and queue backpressure around the shadow execution path so that primary path latency/throughput is not affected and the system stays within SRE-approved capacity budgets.

What this PR does: Adds a budget-aware admission controller in the shadow-runner worker that enforces (1) max in-flight shadow executions, (2) max queued shadow items, and (3) per-route token/sec + request/sec limits (configurable) with sane defaults. Implements backpressure behavior: if the internal queue is above high-watermark, we drop shadow tasks early (pre-enqueue) and emit structured drop reasons rather than letting latency grow unbounded. Adds optional defer mode (bounded retry) for short spikes where queue depth is below a second threshold. Adds metrics + logs for observability and tuning: queue depth, enqueue latency, drop counts by reason, rate-limited counts, and a rolling estimate of shadow compute utilization.

Non-goals: This PR does not change sampling policy selection (RoutePolicy), judge scoring, or payload redaction. It also does not introduce cross-region redistribution; budgets are local to the runner pool.

Behavior details: Admission happens after primary response completion (still async), but before we allocate any GPU slots for shadow. If admission fails, we drop immediately and record shadow_eval.drop_count{reason=...}. Rate limiting uses a token-bucket keyed by (project_id, route_id, shadow_target_id) with optional override to aggregate by (project_id, route_id) when cardinality controls are enabled. The queue uses bounded channel semantics; enqueue attempts past the capacity return a DropQueueFull reason. Backpressure policy: - queue_depth >= high_watermark: drop new items (no enqueue) - queue_depth between soft_limit and high_watermark: allow enqueue but disable defer retries - queue_depth < soft_limit: allow enqueue; retry transient admission failures up to max_defer_ms.

Config knobs (all optional; defaults are conservative): shadow_runner.max_in_flight (default 64 per worker pool), shadow_runner.queue_capacity (default 10k), shadow_runner.queue_soft_limit (default 6k), shadow_runner.queue_high_watermark (default 8k), shadow_runner.defer.max_ms (default 200), shadow_runner.budgets.default_rps (default 5 rps per route), shadow_runner.budgets.default_tps (default 2k tokens/s per route). Per-route overrides via existing RouteConfig override map are supported.

Testing: Unit tests for token bucket + drop reasons; integration tests that simulate bursty enqueue and ensure no blocking on primary request spans; load-test harness config added for SRE validation (see ENG-2440).

Rollout plan: ship behind shadow_runner.budgets.enabled flag (default on in staging, off in prod for first deploy), enable in prod with conservative defaults, then gradually relax caps for beta accounts after SRE sign-off. Kill switch behavior unchanged: kill switch still bypasses shadow execution entirely.

Notes: Metrics tag sets are aligned with observability standards (no user-level identifiers). Drop reason enums are stable and intended for dashboards/alerts.

Snippet (illustrative):
- if queueDepth >= highWatermark -> drop("QUEUE_HIGH_WATERMARK")
- else if !tokenBucket.Allow(costTokens, now) -> drop("RATE_LIMITED")
- else enqueue(item)

References: ENG-2440 (capacity budgets/load tests), Shadow Traffic architecture spec (shadow runner async path).

shadow-runner: token-bucket limiter keyed by project/route/target

conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Can we guarantee that when queue is saturated we don’t introduce any blocking on the primary request goroutine? Please point to the code path where we detach.

Cole Summers (author): Yes. The shadow enqueue happens after primary response is already written; enqueue is non-blocking and returns immediately on saturation. In runner_loop.go we moved shadow scheduling onto a separate worker pool with a bounded channel; primary path only calls TrySubmit() which is O(1) and never waits.
Emily Zhao (review): Rate limiter key includes shadow_target_id. That could blow up cardinality if someone configures many targets. Any guardrails?

Cole Summers (author): Good call. Added config shadow_runner.budgets.keying_mode with default AGGREGATE_BY_ROUTE when cardinality controls are enabled. Also added a hard cap on unique limiter keys per process (default 5k) with LRU eviction; evictions emit shadow_eval.limiter_evictions.
Dylan Brooks (review): For Console dashboards we need drop reason enums to be stable. Please document the set and avoid renames.

Cole Summers (author): Added docs/internal/shadow-traffic/ops/budgets-and-backpressure.md with the enum list and a note that these are part of the telemetry contract. Also added a test that asserts the reason string set doesn’t change accidentally.
Keiko Yamamoto (review): Defer mode worries me: retries can amplify load. Are retries bounded and disabled under backpressure?

Cole Summers (author): Yes—max_defer_ms defaults to 200ms and is disabled entirely once queue_depth >= queue_soft_limit. Also defer retries never allocate GPU; they just re-attempt admission with jitter.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add an on-call note for what to do if we see queue depth alarms. Kill switch vs lowering caps?

Cole Summers (author): Added runbook section to the ops doc: first action is lower per-route budgets (dynamic config) or disable budgets.enabled if it’s causing false drops; if GPU pressure persists, kill switch shadow traffic globally. Follow-up to wire into the formal runbook in a separate PR.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Looks good with the non-blocking guarantee + key aggregation. Please ensure alerts are tuned to page only on sustained drops at low sampling.
Emily Zhao (approval): Approved after LRU cap + docs.
